title: Rav Chanina bar Avin
author: Aharon Hyman
attribution: Model-assisted translation, editorially reviewed; publication authorized by Joshua Waxman.

paragraphs: Hyman observes that throughout the Talmud he is mentioned together with his brother Abaye, and both were Rabbah’s students, as in Pesachim 34a: Abaye bar Avin and Rav Chananya bar Avin were studying Terumot in Rabbah’s school; Rava bar Mattenah met them and said to them, “What do you say about Terumot of the Master’s school?” … They said to him, “Thus said Rabbah.” Abaye was their colleague, as we find in Eruvin 65a and 89a and Bava Batra 87b: “Abaye bar Avin and Rabbi Chanina bar Avin were sitting, and Abaye was sitting with them, and they were saying.” We likewise find them both together in the phrase “both of them say,” as in Berakhot 29b, Shabbat 86b, Eruvin 87b and Yevamot 108a and 119b; there, at 36a, it reads Abaye bar Abba and Rabbi Chinena bar Abaye, and Hyman proposes Abaye bar Avin and Rabbi Chanina bar Avin. Likewise in Keritot 20a it reads “Ami bar Avin and Rabbi Chananya bar Avin,” and Hyman proposes Abaye bar Avin, etc.

notes.text: Abaye bar Avin, his brother Chanina and their colleague Abaye are distinct participants in this source. Saved Davidson Bava Batra87b explicitly writes Rabbi Chanina bar Avin, so the supplied Rabbi form is retained despite the Rav heading. Hyman’s corrective proposals remain attributed.

The consulted Bava Batra 87b passage continues at 88a and directly names Abaye bar Avin and Rabbi Chanina bar Avin as joint speakers. Their brotherhood, Hyman’s throughout-the-Talmud observation and his proposed Abba/Abaye/Ami emendations are retained as his account, without merging them with their colleague Abaye.
